entities.summary: Miguel Ángel Builes Gómez was a Colombian Roman Catholic prelate who served as the Bishop of Santa Rosa de Osos from 1924 until his death. He was the founder of the Xaverian Missionaries of Yarumal (1927) and the Missionaries of Saint Thérèse (1929) as well as the Contemplative Sisters of the Blessed Sacrament (1939) and the Daughters of Our Lady of Mercy (1951). Builes was a prolific writer of pastoral letters and he condemned a vast range of issues in Colombian life that he deemed to be either too liberal or in breach of traditional doctrine; among those he condemned were women wearing trousers and various dance forms.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Builes' condemnation of liberal issues and traditional doctrine had a significant impact on Colombian society, particularly in the areas of women's dress and dance. His writings influenced the country's social norms for decades.
